naming: Every loader builds its YamlDotNet IDeserializer with new DeserializerBuilder().WithNamingConvention(CamelCaseNamingConvention.Instance).IgnoreUnmatchedProperties().Build(). A C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. Dictionary keys are never renamed by the convention. Enum-like string values are parsed case-insensitively; some (like load.mode) additionally strip - and _ before matching, confirmed per-case in the file-flow census (docs/reference/flow/keys.json), not assumed for these new document kinds.

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.

The file(s) the triggered external compute (ADF pipeline / Automation runbook) lands, declared purely for lineage: an invoke moves no catalog data of its own, so this is what connects it to a downstream flowType: file ingestion that reads the same file(s). Binds InvokeBlockYaml.Output (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/InvokeYaml.cs) to InvokeOutputYaml, mapped by FileOutputMapping.Map into InvokeDefinition.Output (src/SqlFlow.Core/Invoke/InvokeOutput.cs). At declared-tier collection FlowSetCollector records the invoke as a file producer and, once the whole estate is scanned, reconciles it against every file ingestion's source spec with the shared engine-parity matcher (src/SqlFlow.Core/Files/FileSelection.cs): on a match the invoke is attributed a Writes of the SAME file node the ingestion Reads, so the merged graph chains invoke -> file -> landing table -> view -> downstream and the execution waves order the fetch before the load. The match is path-first then file (a wildcard always searches within a folder) and conservative (an unconfirmable link yields no edge). Only a standalone flowType: inv document contributes this lineage; on an invokes: entry used as a pre/post hook the hook already orders the run and the inline invoke is not itself a lineage node.

Bound from InvokeDocumentYaml.OnErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.Yaml/InvokeYaml.cs:15) and combined with the invoke block's own value in YamlInvokeFlowLoader.Map: OnErrorResume = y.OnErrorResume ?? invokeYaml.OnErrorResume ?? true (YamlInvokeFlowLoader.cs:84). The resulting InvokeDefinition.OnErrorResume (src/SqlFlow.Core/Invoke/InvokeDefinition.cs:39) is consulted in two reachable seams, neither of which is a direct sqlflow run/validate of this same document: (1) DefaultInvokeRunner.RunByAliasAsync, when this InvokeDefinition is dispatched as another flow's preInvokeAlias/postInvokeAlias hook; a failed dispatch raises and fails the parent flow unless OnErrorResume is true, in which case the failed InvokeResult is returned and the parent continues (src/SqlFlow.Core/Invoke/IInvokeRunner.cs:60-64); and (2) the legacy full-mode FullModeIngestionHost.RunInvokeBatchAsync Batch-grouped run, which stops iterating on the first failure unless OnErrorResume is true (src/SqlFlow.SqlServer/FullMode/FullModeIngestionHost.cs:265-266). A direct CLI run of this standalone document (DocumentExecutor.ExecuteInvokeAsync; src/SqlFlow.Execution/DocumentExecutor.cs:382-412) does not consult it at all: the single dispatch's own success/failure is reported and exit-coded regardless, since there is nothing else in a one-flow run to resume past. A YAML flowType: batch document that includes this file as a member likewise does not consult it: whether a failing member is fatal to that batch is governed entirely by the batch document's own ignoreErrors glob list matched against the member's file path (BatchOrchestrator.ResolveMembers; src/SqlFlow.Orchestration/BatchOrchestrator.cs:238-247), independent of the member's own onErrorResume value.
